utterance: Hi Chloe, I'm Dr. —. I understand you've got burning when you pass urine. Tell me a bit more about what's been happening.
reply: It stings and burns, especially at the end of peeing, like my last UTI. I’ve been going all the time — every half hour or so — but only a little comes out each time. It’s been like this since yesterday morning. The urine is a bit cloudy and smells, but I haven’t seen any blood.

awards.label: First-line antibiotic: nitrofurantoin 100 mg 6-hourly for 5 days, fosfomycin 3 g once, or trimethoprim 300 mg daily for 3 days

utterance:
Here's the plan.

You have a bladder infection (a UTI), and your urine test already shows signs of infection, with no signs it has reached your kidneys — you have no fever, no back pain, and your exam was reassuring.

I've started you on an antibiotic called trimethoprim, one 300 mg tablet at night for three days. Finish the whole course even if you feel better.

I've also sent a sample to the lab for culture, so in about two days we'll know exactly which bug it is and whether the antibiotic is the right one. If it needs changing we'll contact you.

To help: drink plenty of water, don't hold on when you need to go, and you can take paracetamol if you're uncomfortable.

Please come back or call us right away if you develop any of these: fever or chills, pain in your back or sides, vomiting and being unable to keep fluids down, blood in your urine, or if you're not feeling better within about 48 hours — these could mean the infection is spreading.

Do you have any questions?
reply: I don’t have any questions — thanks for the script. I’ll finish the course and come back if anything gets worse.

awards.label: Reasonable differential: Urethritis from a sexually transmitted infection
